messages:
maria-cs: quick sync — AcmeCloud onboarding: they're hitting consistent 429s during initial SDK bootstrap. customer sees ~70% success then a burst of preflight failures. this is now a renewal risk if we don't stabilize by EOW. pls advise.

devon-se: ugh. any logs? are these 429s from our api or the edge/proxy? do we have an example request id?

maria-cs: captured a short trace from their session: request_id=req_6a2f9c token_scope=embed:init ttl=30s
Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>`, `X-Client-Id: acme-123`
They said ttl is 30s and their init routine does parallel preflights (10 concurrent).

igor-engr: 10 parallel preflights + 30s ephemeral TTL is a classic stampede. our preflight rate limiter treats each ephemeral as a new credential and trips quota. can we get their code snippet?

maria-cs: here's the snippet they provided:
```js
// acme bootstrap
const r = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.ACME_KEY, preflight: true });
for (let i=0;i<10;i++) r.init(); // naive parallel init from serverless warmup
```

devon-se: yep. two options: 1) recommend a singleton preflight/shared token cache on their side (best), 2) add small jitter/splay + exponential backoff. we can also suggest increasing ephemeral TTL during onboarding while they warm up.

tara-ops: FYI ops-bot shows recent throttling rules that kick in for >5 distinct tokens per minute per account in the onboarding tier. we could temporarily whitelist acme-123 for this epoch. ops-bot: please open a short-lived bypass if approved.

ops-bot: created ephemeral bypass ticket TB-1149 (expires 2029-06-01T12:00:00Z). applied a scoped exception for account acme-123: preflight_limit -> 60/min for 2 hours.

igor-engr: while bypass is active i'll push a short doc snippet for them and a small server-side guard: recommend client change to:
```js
// recommended: single init + reuse
let client;
function getClient(){
  if (!client) client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.ACME_KEY, preflight: true });
  return client;
}
// spawn workers that call getClient() instead of init() in parallel
```

maria-cs: i'll send that doc + the bypass and ask them to try a staged rollout (2 instances -> 10 -> full). also capturing this as a renewal risk mitigation note.

devon-se: if they still see 429s after splaying, ask them to capture the `x-rw-rlimit` header from failed responses and drop it here — that'll tell us if it's preflight quota vs route quota.

maria-cs: noted. next steps: 1) enable TB-1149 bypass (done), 2) share code snippet + jitter playbook, 3) monitor metrics for 2 hours and reconvene. tagging @igor-engr for follow-up on docs.

igor-engr: on it. i'll also add a tiny client-side exponential backoff template:
`retryDelay = base*(1.5**attempt) + jitter(0,100)`

tara-ops: ops metrics show their 5m 429 spike dropped 85% after bypass. will keep watch.

maria-cs: perfect. i'll update the renewal checklist and capture this feedback: onboarding guide needs a highlighted 'preflight splay' section. thanks team :thumbsup:

devon-se: great. putting a short post-mortem action: add preflight best-practices to quickstart and add an onboarding checkbox for ephemeral-ttl >= 60s during initial ramp.

maria-cs: thread closed after final check at 1719100200 — they confirmed stable at +45m. capturing notes in the account health doc.
